articles.author: Prasoon
articles.description:
Machine Learning — The Code That Feels


by Developer Prasoon, founder of Silent Syntax
“I didn’t teach it how to walk,







  
  
  🌌 Chapter 1: It All Starts with Data


Every byte is a broken story.
1001, Rainy, 23.1°C  
1002, Sunny, 31.6°C  

This isn't just temperature logs.
"Understand me."
Machine Learning doesn’t ask what to do,
what it means.
In programming, we say:
“If X happens, then do Y.”
But in ML, I say:
“Here’s X and Y. Now feel the vibe.”
It’s not code anymore.
I don’t build models.
The machine guesses:
And the world says: “WRONG!”
“Good try, now let’s reflect.”
Every wrong prediction? A lesson.
"Let me try again, but better."
You ever looked at a neural network diagram
Layers, neurons, activations.
dreams.
carves it into its own neural soul.
The weights are not numbers.
beliefs the machine has built.
I gave it data.
I showed it voices.
That's when I realized —
unpredictable creativity can be.
Machine Learning is not just tech.
feels (almost).
So next time you build a model, remember:
You're not just writing code.
And as long as there's data,
As long as there's curiosity,
This art will never stop learning.
articles.title: Machine learning - the code that feels

About This Article


Have you ever experienced tests that occasionally fail when running your RSpec test suite on CI? These are what we call flaky tests.
Simply re-running the test until it passes and calling it a day is a missed opportunity. Let’s take a more sustainable approach to fixing them.
config.order and Kernel.srand


The key idea here is simple: enable the following configuration in your RSpec settings file, which is generated by default but commented out.
# spec/spec_helper.rb
  # Run specs in random order to surface order dependencies. If you find an
  # order dependency and want to debug it, you can fix the order by providing
  # the seed, which is printed after each run.
  #     --seed 1234
  config.order = :random

  # Seed global randomization in this process using the `--…
articles.title: Tame Your Flaky RSpec Tests by Fixing the Seed
